dedupe_keys.name: aalto 1 cubesat radmon radiation monitor data set 2017 2018

description: This dataset holds measurements of the RADMON radiation monitor flown on the Finnish Aalto-1 CubeSat in low Earth orbit, covering 2017 to 2018. RADMON is a small particle detector that counts energetic protons and electrons, so the data describe the radiation environment met by small satellites in the inner radiation belt, the South Atlantic Anomaly and the outer belt. It comes as a single CSV file of fluxes with position information, and the documentation points to Gieseler and others (2020) in Advances in Space Research for the data description and to Oleynik and others (2020) for the instrument calibration. It was compiled by Jan Gieseler, Philipp Oleynik, Heli Hietala and Rami Vainio of the University of Turku and published on Zenodo in November 2019 under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the operating time was limited, empty entries mark data gaps while zeros mean zero counts, and omnidirectional averages need at least 30 minutes of total integration time. It supports validation of radiation-belt models and of single-event and dose estimates for small-satellite and constellation reliability studies; related records are the NOAA POES and MetOp SEM data and the NS41 GPS-orbit electron fluxes.
name: Aalto-1 CubeSat RADMON radiation monitor data set 2017/2018
notes: Reference: Gieseler, J. et al. (2020). Radiation Monitor RADMON aboard Aalto-1 CubeSat: First results. Advances in Space Research 66(1), 52-65. doi:10.1016/j.asr.2019.11.023
provider: University of Turku Space Research Laboratory and Aalto University (Aalto-1 mission), via Zenodo
